featured_reviews.name: Omkar Naik
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dan Dan Chinese today on the occasion of Ram Navami, as many nearby Chinese food corners were closed. I decided to give this place a try, and I ordered two dishes: American Choupsey and Chicken Hakka Noodles.

Both dishes were delicious, and I must say, it was my first time trying Choupsey, which I highly recommend to anyone visiting this place. The Chicken Hakka Noodles were also tasty, and they offer good quality and quantity. The portion sizes are quite generous, so one person may struggle to finish a dish — it's best to come with a companion or plan to parcel the leftover food.

As a local guide on Google Maps and someone who likes to share detailed reviews, I'd like to highlight a few points that may be helpful for potential customers, and also for the owner to consider:

1. Lack of Air Conditioning: There is no air conditioning in the restaurant, and in the humid climate of Vile Parle East, it can get uncomfortable, especially near the fan area. Adding an air conditioning system could significantly improve the dining experience.

2. Cold Drinks: The restaurant doesn't offer cold drinks on the menu but provides them by bringing them from an outside source. While I appreciate that they offer this option when many others refuse, it would be more convenient if they stocked cold drinks on-site.

3. Slow Service: The food took quite a long time to be served, and there was no dedicated staff member to assist customers. There was an uncle helping out, but he was juggling multiple tasks — taking orders, answering calls, handling the kitchen, and managing bills. This made the service a bit frustrating at times, and I ended up packing my noodles to go. It would be beneficial to have an extra staff member to assist with customer service.

4. Mosquitoes: The restaurant is open, and with no gates, mosquitoes can be a problem. The plants outside, while adding to the aesthetic, also provide a hiding place for mosquitoes. Addressing this issue, perhaps with a net or better control, would improve the comfort of diners.

5. Order Assistance: Typically, restaurants guide customers on specials, combos, and menu items when taking orders. However, I was not informed about the combos or daily specials until after my order was placed. It would be helpful if the staff proactively shared this information to enhance the dining experience.

6. Customer Service: While the food was good, there were some basic service issues. No one asked if I wanted water, and there were no tissues or sauces available on the table. That said, I’d like to commend the uncle at the counter, who made an effort to clean my plate, spoon, and fork before serving. His politeness and attention to detail were appreciated.

Suggestions for Improvement:

Install air conditioning to improve comfort in the humid climate.

Stock cold drinks on-site to make it more convenient for customers.

Reduce the waiting time and consider adding more staff for customer service.

Address the mosquito issue, perhaps with better pest control or netting.

Ensure that customers are informed about specials and combos when ordering.

Provide basic amenities like water, tissues, and sauces to enhance the overall dining experience.

Overall, Dan Dan Chinese offers tasty food, but there are some areas for improvement, especially regarding service, comfort, and customer care. With a few adjustments, it could provide a much more enjoyable dining experience.

Note: I’ve added photos of the restaurant, the food I ordered, and the menu for reference to help others get a better idea before visiting.

featured_reviews.name: Dipesh Malvade
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a fan of Indo-Chinese street food, Om Uncle’s Chinese Corner in Marol is a spot you can’t miss! 🏮✨ I finally visited this famous joint and tried their Triple Fried Rice, and here’s my detailed experience.

Food 🍽️:

The Triple Fried Rice was absolutely packed with flavors! 😋 A perfect mix of fried rice, noodles, and crispy noodles on top, all tossed in a spicy, tangy sauce. The balance of textures—soft rice, chewy noodles, and crispy toppings—made every bite exciting. The quantity was generous, making it a great option for sharing. They don’t hold back on flavors, so expect a bold, spicy, and satisfying experience! 🌶️🔥

Ambience & Crowd 🏠:

The place has a classic street-food vibe—nothing too fancy but clean and functional. The seating is minimal, so be ready to wait, especially during peak hours. It was super crowded, which speaks volumes about its popularity! 🏃‍♂️💨 If you’re someone who enjoys the hustle and bustle of a busy food spot, you’ll love the energy here!

Service ⏳:

Despite the crowd, service was quick and efficient. The staff is friendly, and they make sure orders are served fresh and hot. Since it's a small setup, don’t expect fine-dining comfort, but for a street-food joint, it’s well-managed.

Price 💰:

Very affordable for the portion size and taste. You get value for money, making it a great spot for a budget-friendly, tasty meal.

Verdict ⭐:

✅ Must-try for Indo-Chinese lovers
✅ Great flavors & quantity
✅ Crowded but worth it
⚠️ Limited seating & wait time

If you’re in Marol and craving some spicy, flavorful Chinese street food, this place should be on your list! Would definitely visit again. 🥢🔥

featured_reviews.name: Akshay Davda
featured_reviews.review_text:
GC is a Pure Veg resturant opposite andheri shoppers stop. GC was very helpful to arrange a table for 14 which included 10 adults & 4 kids on Saturday night ( 21.4.18 ) on very short notice whereas most places were either packed or couldn’t arrange seating for tis number .

Must Have from our order :-
Manchow Soup, Dry Manchurian, Dry Paneer chilly Veg Mastana, Rotis over Kulcha , Malai kulfi .

Our extensive order was as follows :-
Soup
1) Tomato Soup - Kids
2) Sweet Corn Soup - kids
3) Hot N Sour Soup - Very Nice
4) Manchow Soup - Super . Best among the lot
5) Cream of Veg - Decent

Starters
1) Dry Manchurian :- Superb
2) Paneer Chilly :- paneer was soft & sauces were spicy as per our request .
3) Spring Roll :- Average . Compared to the other two tis dish was a let down .

Main Course :-
Indian
1) Veg Mastana :- Tis Veg was amazing .
2) Daal Makhani ( Black Daal ) :- Was bland & a let down.
3) butter tandoori Roti turned out better than the kulcha .
4) Masala Papad :- Decent
Chinese Main course
1) Veg Hakka Noodles :- Mainly for the kids as a non spicy option but for adults it was quite bland
2) Triple Schezwan Rice :- Wasn’t spicy enough but overall a decent item

Desserts :-
1) Falooda :- quality & quantity decent but quite sweet for my liking .
2) Malai Kulfi :- sweetness was balanced & enjoyed tis more than the Falooda

Overall Review :-
Location :- Very Nice & easily accessible
Valet parking available which is a huge relief otherwise you would have to park around or in shoppers stop especially during weekends.
Ambience :- Simple & Decent ( nothing fancy )
Staff :- Very Polite & cooperative
( Our Table Supervisor & Server were very helpful in food selection  & dint create a fuss about the noise made by us ) - Added his pic 👍
Service :- Average wasn’t fast but neither too slow
Food Quality :- Decent
Food Quantity :- Very Good
Food Taste :- Soup & starters were very nice .
Main course go for Indian over Chinese .

VFM :- 4/5 . Our soup & starters turned out better than our main course.

featured_reviews.name: Riya
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently visited Cray Craft and it just felt like a paradise for people who love good food and interiors. The facade was majestic, a double height restaurant with warm interiors so pretty that your gallery would be full of pictures. As for the food, it was delicious. I started with their mocktails, Whisper of the tribe and Leopard s’lullaby. Both the drinks felt so refreshing and the tropical flavours in them were standing out. For appetizers, I got the Xiao Long Soup Dimsum, and I need to tell you how it was so juicy, bursting with juices and stuffed with chicken. Next I tried their sichuan pepper toss chicken and I think this is one of the best appetizers I have got. For mains, I got chicken blue pea rice with japanese curry. This was something I tried for the first time and I love good the curry went with the rice. As a person who loooves ramen, I had to get their grilled sambhal chicken miso ramen. It was loaded with veggies, eggs, chicken, mushrooms, and a warm broth, just what you need on a tough day. Ofcourse I couldn’t leave without trying their tiramisu, which they made live on my table. The creamy mascarpone and the cocoa powder, wow, the ladyfingers soaked all the espresso, the first bite felt like I was in dessert heaven. Truly it’s a nice place to visit with your friends, family or your date. So I would definately recommend you this restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: Nihar Rathod
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐☆☆☆☆ (1 Star) – Very Disappointing Experience at Tipsy Tiger

I recently visited The Tipsy Tiger expecting a good Japanese dining experience, but unfortunately, it turned out to be quite disappointing.

The biggest issue was the ambience. The restaurant looks much better in the photos than it does in reality. The overall vibe felt dull and lifeless, and the place lacked the atmosphere you would expect from a restaurant of this category.

Another major concern was the ventilation. The restaurant is non-AC, and the airflow was extremely poor, making the environment feel hot, stuffy, and exhausting. Despite raising the issue multiple times with the staff and management, no meaningful action was taken to improve the situation or address our concerns.

As for the food, it was average at best (2.5/5). We ordered:

Steamed Wonton Chicken

Tiger Chilly Chicken

Spicy Prawns Tempura (4 pcs)

Yakitori Classics

Chicken Spring Roll

Chicken Katsu Bao

None of the dishes stood out or justified the pricing. The flavors were ordinary, and I expected much better quality and authenticity from a restaurant claiming to serve Japanese cuisine.

The only positive aspect was the service, which was timely and courteous. The staff served the food promptly, but good service alone could not make up for the poor ambience, ventilation issues, and average food quality.

Overall, if you're looking for a place to enjoy good Japanese food and a lively dining experience, I would not recommend Tipsy Tiger. The combination of poor ventilation, underwhelming food, and a dead atmosphere made for a very disappointing visit.

Food: 2.5/5
Ambience: 1/5
Service: 4/5
Overall Experience: 1/5

featured_reviews.review_text:
​If you are looking for high-quality Pan-Asian cuisine in the Andheri/Sakinaka area, Asia Kitchen remains one of the most reliable spots. It manages to balance a sophisticated dining atmosphere with a menu that feels both authentic and approachable.
​The Ambiance
The decor is modern and sleek, making it equally suitable for a formal business lunch or a relaxed dinner with family.
​The Food
The menu is a well-curated journey through Chinese, Japanese, and Southeast Asian flavors. Some standout highlights include:
​Dim Sums: The crust is consistently delicate, and the fillings—especially the Truffle Edamame—are flavorful and fresh.
​Sushi: For those who enjoy Japanese, the Salmon and Avocado rolls are well-constructed and use high-grade ingredients.
​Main Course: The Chicken Thai Green Curry is aromatic and perfectly balanced, pairing beautifully with Jasmine rice. Their signature Szechuan Noodles offer that classic fiery kick without being overwhelming.
​The Service
The staff is generally attentive and well-versed in the menu. They are happy to provide recommendations based on your spice tolerance and dietary preferences, which adds a personalized touch to the meal.
​The Verdict
While it sits at a slightly higher price point than your average local eatery, the consistency in taste and the upscale environment justify the cost. It’s a great pick for anyone in Mumbai wanting a dependable, delicious Asian feast.
​Pro Tip: It can get quite busy on weekend evenings, so booking a table in advance is highly recommended.

However it is non Ac so people can have right expectations before coming. Everything is freshly made and is yummy. Quantity is more than sufficient. Loved it, will definitely come again 🤩

featured_reviews.name: Spoons of Mumbai
featured_reviews.review_text: We visited this nice shack right beside Goregaon station in west. This is an only Chinese food place but they do serve pasta. Purely vegetarian and You do get a lot of Jain variety as well. We started with veg clear soup and ordered veg lollipop for the starters, and then followed by Paneer Manchurian and Paneer triple rice in the main course. The service was very good and quick and the value for money was excellent as well. All in all the food tasted better and I recommend this to all the vegetarian food lovers as a must visit.

featured_reviews.name: Manish Dhanavade
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tasty Food, Poor Quantity and Staff Attitude

I visited the Wow China outlet at Oberoi Mall and the food was genuinely good in terms of taste and quality. However, the quantity served was quite less for the price. I shared this feedback politely at the counter, but the staff member did not receive it well and denied the issue completely, which was disappointing. A little more openness to customer feedback would really improve the overall experience.

featured_reviews.name: Aarzoo Malhotra
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had chicken Khao Suey for the first time and didn't know it is a coconut milk based dish. I am not a fan of coconut based dishes so it was okayish for me. I expected the dish to be assembled but they gave everything separate. Soup was very heavy and thick like gravy, but still I'd say price is on the expensive side for a medium serving of noodle soup.
It was a filling meal.
Wait time was too much. It took more than 30 minutes.
Staff was polite.
I'd give it 3 stars because of my personal preference.

featured_reviews.name: Arun Pasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I ordered food and waited for 40 minutes. When I went to the store to check, they informed me that the item was out of stock and asked me to wait another 30 minutes.

I then called the helpline number, where the representative told me I would receive my order within 10 minutes. However, the store staff continued to say it would take 30 minutes.

Since there was no stock available, I requested a refund. I was told that there is no refund option in the mobile application and that they could not process a refund. Instead, they insisted that I continue waiting. They also said that if I did not receive the food later, then they would “think about it.”

Kimchi, omg, it had ketchup in it

Some momos are decent but not all.

They really need to work on their recipes.

Poor taste over-all and on top of that the service is very very slow.

My first and last time visiting this place
